findings.claim: The proposed single case cannot reproduce all six aliases because bm-2s has a different completion instrument and gate contract. Treating instruments and the gate as case-owned makes bm-2s either provision the wrong executable or forces configuration-specific task policy back into the configuration.
findings.evidence: benchmark/specs/bm-2s/manifest.json:236-245 declares threshold >=26 and its count-gate semantics, while benchmark/specs/bm-2d/manifest.json:244-252 declares >=1; benchmark/provision.sh:213-226 copies the manifest-selected instruments and benchmark/provision.sh:257-268 requires the gate contract fields. The shipped bm-2s/gate.sh hash is 66ba1c4f..., whereas bm-1, bm-2, bm-2d, and bm-2dc use 3cfab221.... The design nevertheless assigns one case.mission and one instrument set at metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:95-110,129-134 and asserts exact reconstruction at :208-211.
findings.fix: Model bm-2s as a distinct case/version or explicitly introduce a versioned task-instrument variant owned by the case. Add a fixture that compares instrument bytes as well as the generated contract and metasystem.conf for every alias.

findings.claim: Relabelling bm-1 as taskrun@0.2 is not an honest identity migration: bm-1's 0.1 gate is not the same case artifact as bm-2s's 0.2 count gate, and aliases would rewrite archived evidence to an identity it never ran.
findings.evidence: benchmark/specs/bm-1/manifest.json:2-6 identifies bm-1@0.1; benchmark/specs/bm-1/manifest.json:301-309 defines its >=1 gate. benchmark/specs/bm-2s/manifest.json:236-245 defines the materially different >=26 gate and benchmark/specs/bm-2s/manifest.json:311 labels it 0.2. Current extraction verifies stamped identity against the installed manifest at benchmark/extractor.py:481-492. The proposed alias deliberately maps bm-1 to taskrun@0.2 while merely noting the historical 0.1 label at metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:196-199.
findings.fix: Preserve bm-1 as an alias to taskrun@0.1 and represent the count-gate change as taskrun@0.2, or retain immutable legacy identity alongside normalized pair identity. Never make an alias claim that old evidence executed a different case version.

findings.claim: The comparability redesign is incomplete and could weaken the current tuple to only the case/config pair. Equal pair identities are necessary but not sufficient: current verdicts also require equal kit version, roster, fences, repetition count, machine fingerprint, and measuring metasystem SHA. Conversely, the proposed report axis for differing configurations cannot use compare.py's current verdict path because it intentionally rejects any tuple difference.
findings.evidence: benchmark/compare.py:164-175 defines the full current comparability tuple; benchmark/compare.py:220-225 enforces it within cohorts and benchmark/compare.py:523-527 across cohorts. metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:66-71 says metasystem comparisons require identical case/config and configuration comparisons are a report axis, but :151-153 only says the check 'uses the pair' without preserving the remaining tuple or defining the separate report path.
findings.fix: Specify two explicit algorithms: metasystem verdict comparison must require equal caseId/version, configId/version, kit version, repetition count, machine fingerprint, measuring metasystem SHA, and sealed effective roster/fences; configuration comparison must be a separate non-verdict command/output that permits config differences while stating which remaining controls must match.

findings.claim: Proposal and result migration is underspecified and will break evolution comparisons. Current proposals name a list of bare spec IDs, compare.py tests membership, loads the installed manifest by that ID, and emits bare specs. Merely changing scorecard identity and saying proposals name pairs leaves the proposal schema, lookup rules, output schema version, and fixtures ambiguous.
findings.evidence: benchmark/evolution-fixtures.sh:50-64 creates a proposal with specs:["fixture"]; benchmark/compare.py:259-300 validates that exact list shape; benchmark/compare.py:529-538 tests the bare ID and loads benchmark/specs/<id>/manifest.json; benchmark/compare.py:568-581 emits schemaVersion 1 and specs containing a bare ID. The design offers two incompatible pair representations—strings or structured objects—at metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:151-153.
findings.fix: Choose one canonical structured proposal representation, version proposal and compare-result records, define pair membership and installed-case/config lookup precisely, migrate the evolution fixture through eligible, ineligible, mismatch, and ancestry paths, and define read behavior for legacy proposal/result schemaVersion 1.

findings.claim: Deleting specs immediately after teaching aliases strands in-flight cohorts. Resume state persists only specId, reconstructs benchmark/specs/<specId>, derives mission ID and contract path from it, and later runs that spec's grader. An alias-aware start path does not repair already-created state or already-signed mission-bm-*.contract.md files.
findings.evidence: benchmark/run-cohort.sh:220-230 writes specId into state; benchmark/run-cohort.sh:253-270 reads it, resolves benchmark/specs/$spec_id, and derives mission-$spec_id.contract.md; benchmark/run-cohort.sh:282-312 resumes and grades that mission. Migration deletes specs in step 3 at metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:178-179 without an in-flight drain or state migration.
findings.fix: Inventory and drain active cohorts before deletion, or keep immutable legacy spec directories until all are terminal. If migration is supported, add a versioned state transformation preserving the existing mission ID, contract path, grader source, identity stamp, and signed contract rather than resolving the alias to a newly named mission.

findings.claim: The required hostCaps contract makes five of six configurations impossible to derive exactly from current data. Only bm-1 declares hostMaxTurns and hostMaxBudgetUsd; inventing values violates exact reconstruction, while omitting them violates the proposed compatibility law.
findings.evidence: benchmark/specs/bm-1/manifest.json:144-155 contains hostMaxTurns=150 and hostMaxBudgetUsd=5.00. The other manifests' fences omit both fields; for example benchmark/specs/bm-2d/manifest.json:30-39. Current provisioning validates ordinary fence fields at benchmark/provision.sh:292-298 and does not require host caps. The design requires config.hostCaps at metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:118-124 and says host caps must be present at :141-143.
findings.fix: Decide whether host caps are optional capability-specific allowances or mandatory configuration fields. For each legacy alias, specify exact sourced values or an explicit absent value with join behavior; do not synthesize defaults. Add all six cases to the byte-equivalence fixture.

findings.claim: The network vocabulary assigns the same policy to both halves without defining precedence. Current manifests explicitly justify delegateNetwork as per-task policy, while the new design calls it both a task requirement and a configuration policy. The proposed 'satisfies' relation is insufficient for values allowed, denied, and any and could either grant network against task isolation or reject a harmless stricter configuration.
findings.evidence: benchmark/specs/bm-2d/manifest.json:24-28 says delegateNetwork is per-spec and explains task-specific reasons; benchmark/provision.sh:366-368 currently requires the manifest policy directly. The design places needs.delegateNetwork in the case at metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:102-106, environment.delegateNetwork in the configuration at :121-123, and leaves satisfaction undefined at :140.
findings.fix: Separate case requirement from configuration capability with directional names, such as case.networkRequirement and config.networkAllowance. Define the complete compatibility table and specify that the effective envelope uses the stricter compatible value; validate the emitted metasystem.conf permission for every alias.

findings.claim: Moving comparisonEligible wholly to the case silently changes the orchestration-health aliases. Today bm-2d, bm-2dc, and bm-2d-og are permanently ineligible because their acceptance question is adapter health, not merely because the shared task is 0.x. A shared case-level true value after promotion would make those configurations verdict-eligible unless purpose is an explicit second gate.
findings.evidence: benchmark/specs/bm-2d/manifest.json:2-7 combines acceptanceOnly with comparisonEligible=false and states it is never comparison-eligible. Current compare.py derives eligibility only from the installed manifest at benchmark/compare.py:533-544. The design assigns comparisonEligible to the case and purpose to the configuration at metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:72-75, but its compare proposal does not specify that orchestration-health forces no-verdict.
findings.fix: Define verdict eligibility as case.comparisonEligible AND config.purpose==capability, with acceptanceOnly controlling launch cadence rather than score semantics. Add fixtures proving health configurations remain no-verdict after a case reaches 1.0 and that acceptanceOnly configurations cannot enter standing cadence accidentally.

findings.claim: The case/config join drops or ambiguously relocates fields needed for exact contracts: completionGate is listed in case.json but absent from the stated mission join; exposure notes are roster-specific but the configuration sketch cannot preserve the existing missionContract.exposureNote verbatim; mission streams can contradict the selected gate, as bm-2s currently does.
findings.evidence: benchmark/provision.sh:229-239 reads missionContract, fences, completionGate, roster, and environment separately, and benchmark/provision.sh:256-272 requires completionGate.command and missionContract.exposure. benchmark/specs/bm-1/manifest.json:331 contains exposure and its roster-specific note follows in the manifest; benchmark/specs/bm-2s/manifest.json:244-245 has threshold >=26 while :263-265 still tells builders the gate reports self-assessment=1. The proposed join enumerates case.mission, roster, fences, hostCaps, envelope, and exposure at metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:127-134 but omits completionGate and note-preservation rules.
findings.fix: Provide a complete field-by-field projection table from every current manifest JSON pointer to case or configuration and then to contract/metasystem.conf. Include completionGate, all notes that must survive, mission ID, environment permissions, instrument source, and a validation rule that streams agree with the selected gate.

findings.claim: The documentation plan lacks the normative schemas, compatibility matrix, versioning rules, and validation workflow needed for an agent on another machine to add a case or configuration safely. A prose list of nouns and commands cannot replace the current manifest's single-authority contract.
findings.evidence: benchmark/README.md:13-19 currently tells readers manifest.json is the single authority for metrics, fences, roster, and mission policy, while benchmark/README.md:32-57 documents only one concrete run. The new design promises README-only authoring at metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:180-185,216-219, but its documentation list does not require field references, required/optional status, compatibility truth tables, version-bump criteria, alias restrictions, validation commands, instrument semantics, or machine/network behavior.
findings.fix: Require README sections containing complete annotated case.json and configuration JSON examples, schema links and required/optional fields, ownership rules for every field, case/config version-bump rules, compatibility tables for OS/network/fence floors, effective join output, instrument-tag and mission-ID rules, alias immutability, comparison modes, validation commands, and a worked add-case/add-configuration procedure. Add JSON schemas for cases, configurations, aliases, cohorts, proposals, and compare results to the documented validation surface.

findings.claim: Instrument tag naming is not actually unchanged and creates collisions across configurations and legacy identities. Current tags include the spec/configuration-bearing ID; the proposal removes configuration identity. Two configurations of the same case provisioned into related history can therefore claim the same tag despite potentially different legacy instruments, and taskrun@0.2 would falsely label bm-1's 0.1 instrument.
findings.evidence: benchmark/provision.sh:181-186 validates the current manifest ID/version for the tag, benchmark/provision.sh:371 emits <specId>-instruments-v<version>, and benchmark/provision.sh:536-540 creates the tag and writes it into the contract. The design calls <caseId>-instruments-v<caseVersion> an 'unchanged shape' at metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:133-134, despite removing the old spec ID and despite the bm-2s instrument difference evidenced by benchmark/specs/bm-2s/manifest.json:236-245.
findings.fix: Make the tag identify the exact immutable instrument bundle, either through a genuine case version that changes whenever any instrument changes or a content-derived bundle version. Specify collision/refusal behavior and test all legacy aliases against the expected tag and instrument bytes.

summary: The design cannot currently preserve the shipped benchmark: bm-2s is a materially different task-instrument version, bm-1 cannot honestly be relabelled 0.2, mandatory host caps are absent from five manifests, and deletion of specs strands resumable cohorts. The comparison contract also needs two explicit modes, a fully versioned proposal/result migration, and preservation of the existing non-identity comparability controls. Before implementation, the design needs a complete source-to-case/config-to-output projection, precise compatibility and verdict rules, honest legacy identity handling, and normative README/schema requirements.
